lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Unit performance task: verifying every rule against a current local source

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic verifying every rule against a current local source task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner assembles the week's category worksheets, process-reading notes, responsibility sorting, and notice-response practice into one checklist, then works with an adult to identify and check at least one item against a current, real, local or official source, explicitly marking any item not yet verified rather than guessing.
safetyNotes: Verifying against a real local source is the goal where genuinely possible, but an honestly marked 'not yet verified' item is an acceptable and expected part of this checklist, not a failure.
This is not legal advice; the task is building and starting to verify a personal checklist, not delivering a definitive legal answer.

simulationAlternative.description: If the learner cannot access or verify a real current local source right now (no adult available, no reliable source at hand, or the source is genuinely unclear), the checklist is completed using the week's general categories only, with every item explicitly marked 'not yet verified against a real source' — this earns full, equal credit, since the assessed skill is knowing what to verify and how, not proof of a completed real-world lookup.

materials: learner-local: the week's earlier artifacts from this unit
learner-local: paper or a notes document

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g12-u04-l06-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g12-u04-l06-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g12-u04-l06-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g12-u04-l06-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Why is a checklist that honestly marks some items as 'not yet verified' more useful than one that guesses at everything to look complete?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g12-u04-l06-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g12-u04-l06-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g12-u04-l06-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Checklist coverage: All four categories are represented on the checklist. | Verification honesty: Every 'verified' item names the real source that was actually checked, and unverified items are honestly marked as such. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g12-u04-l06-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner set a specific date to revisit and verify the remaining unverified items, and explain why that timing makes sense.

resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner assembles the week's category worksheets, process-reading notes, responsibility sorting, and notice-response practice into one checklist, then works with an adult to identify and check at least one item against a current, real, local or official source, explicitly marking any item not yet verified rather than guessing.
Coach direction: Before assembling, predict which checklist item will be hardest to actually verify.
Learner prompt: Looking back at this week's categories, which item do you predict will be hardest to actually verify against a real source, and why?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: verifying every rule against a current local source complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Assemble the checklist from the week's artifacts.
Response 1 (t2-p1): My checklist covers identification, records, registration, and responsibilities categories from this week.
Response 2 (t2-p2): With an adult, I identified at least one item to actually check against a current, real, local or official source, or marked items honestly as not yet verified.

Equal-access rule: If the learner cannot access or verify a real current local source right now (no adult available, no reliable source at hand, or the source is genuinely unclear), the checklist is completed using the week's general categories only, with every item explicitly marked 'not yet verified against a real source' — this earns full, equal credit, since the assessed skill is knowing what to verify and how, not proof of a completed real-world lookup.

resources.title: verifying every rule against a current local source minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Why is a checklist that honestly marks some items as 'not yet verified' more useful than one that guesses at everything to look complete?

Success checks: Checklist coverage: All four categories are represented on the checklist. | Verification honesty: Every 'verified' item names the real source that was actually checked, and unverified items are honestly marked as such.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: verifying every rule against a current local source supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g12-u04-l06-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g12-u04-l06-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional verifying every rule against a current local source condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Checklist coverage: All four categories are represented on the checklist. | Verification honesty: Every 'verified' item names the real source that was actually checked, and unverified items are honestly marked as such..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g12-u04-l06-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
